- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later days — suggest adjusting for mean reversion toward lower levels.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 85+), model tends to overshoot and overreact — reduce forecast by 2–5% for subsequent days following such events.
- Model underestimates true price drops, especially when prices fall below 80 — consider adding a downward bias correction for values below 80.
- Forecast tends to lag true price movements by 1–3 days — adjust for a 1-day lag in price decline or rise.
- Model often fails to capture the “tail” of the price curve — especially in the last 5–7 days — consider smoothing or weighting recent data more heavily.
- When true price is below 75, model tends to be overly optimistic — apply a downward correction of 3–8% depending on proximity to 70.
- Model overreacts to recent volatility — reduce forecast sensitivity to recent 3–5 day price swings.
